# Literacy Compass: target catalogue

Compass v0.1.0: 45 targets on 8 axes. See [04-literacy-compass.md](../04-literacy-compass.md) for how the Compass works.

Evidence ladder: 0 Not found, 1 Stated, 2 Designed, 3 Tested, 4 Measured.

| Axis | Lens | Question |
|---|---|---|
| **INF** Information and media | learner | Does it help learners find, judge and use information and media, including AI-generated content? |
| **COM** Communication, citizenship and rights | learner | Does it help learners interact well, take part as citizens and know their rights? |
| **CRE** Creation and computational thinking | learner | Does it help learners create, remix responsibly and think computationally? |
| **SAF** Safety, privacy and wellbeing | learner | Does it help learners stay safe, protect their data, manage money and balance their use? |
| **PRB** Problem solving and learning to learn | learner | Does it help learners solve problems, choose tools and reflect on their own digital skills? |
| **AI** AI literacy | learner | Does it help learners engage with, create with, manage and shape AI? |
| **TRN** Transparency that teaches | design | Does the product explain itself to children in a way that builds literacy, and avoid teaching the opposite? |
| **EDU** Educator and family enablement | design | Can teachers and families turn use into learning, and see that learning happened? |

## INF: Information and media

*Does it help learners find, judge and use information and media, including AI-generated content?*

### INF-01 Find and choose sources

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners search with a purpose, compare results and choose sources that fit the question.
- **Why:** Searching and filtering is the first DigComp competence and the base of every other information skill.
- **Look for:** Tasks where learners search, filter or pick between sources and explain the choice.
- **Improvement:** Add tasks where learners must search, filter and pick a source, and say why it fits.
- **Ideas:** A detective quest where clues come from sources of different quality; A search challenge with a budget of queries
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 1.1; UNESCO-MIL locate and access information
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [UNESCO-MIL](https://www.unesco.org/en/media-information-literacy)

### INF-02 Judge credibility by checking across sources

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners check who is behind information, compare it with other sources (lateral reading) and decide how far to trust it.
- **Why:** UNESCO's MIL curriculum and its 2026 AI companion guide put source checking and informed trust at the centre.
- **Look for:** Activities that ask learners to verify a claim elsewhere, trace a source or rate credibility with reasons.
- **Improvement:** Turn at least one task into a verification task with a debrief on why trust went up or down.
- **Ideas:** Two-tab challenge that rewards checking a claim on another site before answering; Trust meter with reasons instead of a right answer
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 1.2; UNESCO-MIL critically evaluate information; UNESCO-AIMIL 3.3
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [UNESCO-MIL](https://www.unesco.org/en/media-information-literacy), [UNESCO-AIMIL](https://doi.org/10.58338/JXYO3928)

### INF-03 Recognise persuasion, advertising and commercial intent

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** purchases.
- **Target:** Learners recognise advertising, sponsorship and persuasive design, and can say who benefits.
- **Why:** Children are a protected group under consumer law; recognising commercial intent is part of evaluating information.
- **Look for:** Activities about ads, influencers, sponsored content or persuasive design, with age-appropriate explanations.
- **Improvement:** Add a short activity that unpacks one ad or persuasive pattern the learners meet in daily life.
- **Ideas:** Spot-the-ad level; Learners design an honest and a manipulative version of the same ad and compare
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 1.2; UNESCO-MIL evaluate content of all content providers
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [UNESCO-MIL](https://www.unesco.org/en/media-information-literacy), [UCPD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681)

### INF-04 Spot mis- and disinformation, including synthetic media

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ai_generative, ugc.
- **Target:** Learners recognise false or manipulated content, including AI-generated images, audio and text, and know how to check provenance.
- **Why:** DigComp 3.0 made mis- and disinformation a priority; AILit and UNESCO link it to AI-generated content.
- **Look for:** Tasks with manipulated or generated media, provenance checks, or correcting false claims.
- **Improvement:** Include generated or manipulated examples and teach a check (source, date, reverse search, provenance label).
- **Ideas:** Real-or-generated round with explanations of the tells and their limits; Trace-the-origin puzzle
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 1.2; AILIT Create 4; UNESCO-AIMIL 2.5, 3.3
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AIMIL](https://doi.org/10.58338/JXYO3928), [UNESCO-MIL](https://www.unesco.org/en/media-information-literacy)

### INF-05 Organise, keep and cite information

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** B3, B4, B5.
- **Target:** Learners save, organise and reference what they found so others can check it.
- **Why:** Managing information is a DigComp competence and supports honest use of sources.
- **Look for:** Features or tasks for collecting, organising and citing sources.
- **Improvement:** Let learners keep and cite the sources they used, and reward correct attribution.
- **Ideas:** Evidence board where clues must carry their source; Citation as a game resource
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 1.3
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149)


## COM: Communication, citizenship and rights

*Does it help learners interact well, take part as citizens and know their rights?*

### COM-01 Interact respectfully and with empathy

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** chat, multiplayer, social.
- **Target:** Learners practise respectful, empathetic communication and understand how tone is read online.
- **Why:** Digital behaviour and interaction are DigComp competences; empathy is a DQ (IEEE 3527.1) area.
- **Look for:** Scenarios about tone, misunderstandings, kindness or conflict online, with discussion.
- **Improvement:** Add scenarios where learners choose and discuss how to respond to others online.
- **Ideas:** Rewrite-the-message challenge; Perspective-switch scenes
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 2.1, 2.5; IEEE3527 digital empathy
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [IEEE3527](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/3527.1/7589/)

### COM-02 Collaborate through digital tools

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** multiplayer.
- **Target:** Learners plan, share and build together using digital tools, with roles and shared reflection.
- **Why:** Collaboration is a DigComp competence and a recurrent quality marker for game-based learning.
- **Look for:** Cooperative modes, shared goals, roles, and a debrief of how the group worked.
- **Improvement:** Add a cooperative task with roles and a short reflection on how the team worked.
- **Ideas:** Cooperative puzzles that need every role; Team retrospectives after a mission
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 2.4
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149)

### COM-03 Know and use digital rights; take part as citizens

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners know their rights online (privacy, expression, information, protection) and practise civic participation.
- **Why:** UN General Comment 25 and the UNESCO MIL curriculum frame literacy as a matter of rights and participation.
- **Look for:** Content about children's rights online, freedom of expression, participation or complaints.
- **Improvement:** Add content that names children's rights online and how to use them.
- **Ideas:** Rights cards earned by solving situations; Design a fair rule for an online community
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 2.3; UNESCO-MIL human rights and dignity
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation), [UNESCO-MIL](https://www.unesco.org/en/media-information-literacy)

### COM-04 Respond to hate, harassment and harmful content

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** chat, ugc, social.
- **Target:** Learners recognise hate speech, harassment and harmful content, and know how to respond, report and support others.
- **Why:** The UNESCO MIL curriculum names responding to hate content online as a core competence; BIK+ supports it.
- **Look for:** Scenarios on cyberbullying or hate speech with bystander options and where to get help.
- **Improvement:** Add a scenario on responding to harassment, including reporting and supporting a peer.
- **Ideas:** Upstander choices with consequences; Report-and-support walkthrough
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 2.5; UNESCO-MIL respond to hate and radical content online
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [UNESCO-MIL](https://www.unesco.org/en/media-information-literacy), [BIK](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/strategy-better-internet-kids)

### COM-05 Manage digital identity and footprint

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** accounts, ugc, social, survey.
- **Target:** Learners understand what they leave behind online, how identity is presented and how to manage it.
- **Why:** Managing digital identity is a DigComp competence; footprint management is a DQ competence.
- **Look for:** Activities on profiles, avatars, permanence of posts and what others can see.
- **Improvement:** Show learners what their actions leave behind and let them practise managing it.
- **Ideas:** Footprint trail mechanic that shows what stays; Avatar choices with privacy trade-offs explained
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 2.6; IEEE3527 digital footprint management
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [IEEE3527](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/3527.1/7589/)


## CRE: Creation and computational thinking

*Does it help learners create, remix responsibly and think computationally?*

### CRE-01 Create and express with digital media

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ugc.
- **Target:** Learners make their own digital content (text, images, sound, video, games) for a purpose and an audience.
- **Why:** Developing digital content is a DigComp competence; creating is also how learners understand media from the inside.
- **Look for:** Creation tools, open tasks and sharing with a defined audience.
- **Improvement:** Add an open creation task with a purpose, an audience and feedback.
- **Ideas:** Level editor; Make-a-news-story mode
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 3.1
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149)

### CRE-02 Remix responsibly and give credit

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ugc, ai_generative.
- **Target:** Learners reuse and remix content legally and fairly, understand licences and credit authors, including when AI is involved.
- **Why:** Copyright and licences are a DigComp competence; AILit adds authenticity and intellectual property of AI content.
- **Look for:** Content on licences (for example Creative Commons), attribution, and honest disclosure of AI help.
- **Improvement:** Teach and require attribution when learners reuse assets or AI output.
- **Ideas:** Credits screen learners must fill in; Licence badges on reusable assets
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 3.2, 3.3; AILIT Create 4
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)

### CRE-03 Computational thinking and programming

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners decompose problems, recognise patterns, build algorithms and debug, with or without code.
- **Why:** Computational thinking and programming is a DigComp competence and a foundation for shaping AI.
- **Look for:** Coding, block programming, algorithm puzzles or unplugged activities with debugging.
- **Improvement:** Add tasks where learners build and debug a sequence of instructions.
- **Ideas:** Program-the-robot puzzles; Debug-the-broken-level challenge
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 3.4; AILIT Manage 3
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)


## SAF: Safety, privacy and wellbeing

*Does it help learners stay safe, protect their data, manage money and balance their use?*

### SAF-01 Protect devices and accounts; recognise scams

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** accounts.
- **Target:** Learners use strong passwords or passphrases, recognise phishing and scams, and know what to do when something looks wrong.
- **Why:** Protecting devices is a DigComp competence; DigComp 3.0 prioritised cybersecurity competence.
- **Look for:** Activities on passwords, phishing, scams or suspicious links.
- **Improvement:** Add a short, age-appropriate activity on scams or account protection.
- **Ideas:** Phishing inbox sorting game; Build-a-passphrase challenge
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 4.1; IEEE3527 personal cyber security management
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [IEEE3527](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/3527.1/7589/)

### SAF-02 Understand personal data and privacy choices

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** accounts, ai_adaptive, recommender, survey.
- **Target:** Learners understand what personal data is, who can see it, how products use it, and how to make privacy choices.
- **Why:** Protecting personal data and privacy is a DigComp competence and a right under the GDPR.
- **Look for:** Activities on personal data, permissions, privacy settings, or what the product itself collects.
- **Improvement:** Use the product's own data use as a teaching example, in age-appropriate language.
- **Ideas:** Data trail visualiser of the learner's own session; Permission puzzles
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 4.2; IEEE3527 privacy management; UNESCO-AIMIL 1.2
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [IEEE3527](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/3527.1/7589/)

### SAF-03 Handle contact risks and seek help

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** chat, multiplayer, social, ugc.
- **Target:** Learners know what to do if someone online makes them uncomfortable, including blocking, reporting and telling a trusted adult or helpline.
- **Why:** Contact risks are central to the EU KIDS Act proposal and BIK+; help-seeking is the protective skill.
- **Look for:** Age-appropriate scenarios on contact from strangers or pressure, and named routes to help.
- **Improvement:** Teach the block, report and tell routes, and name a helpline for the learner's country.
- **Ideas:** Trusted-adult map; Practice report flow in a safe sandbox
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 4.1, 4.3
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [BIK](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/strategy-better-internet-kids), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681)

### SAF-04 Balance use and self-regulate

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** streaks, notifications, leaderboards.
- **Target:** Learners notice how digital products capture attention, reflect on their own use and practise taking breaks.
- **Why:** Supporting wellbeing is a DigComp competence; the Education Package launches a European Healthy Screens Pledge.
- **Look for:** Activities on attention design, screen time reflection, or built-in stopping points discussed with learners.
- **Improvement:** Add a reflection on attention design, using the product's own stopping points as the example.
- **Ideas:** Natural end points with a reflection prompt; Attention-trap spotting activity
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 4.3
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [EU-EDUPKG](https://doi.org/10.2766/6358386), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681)
- **Hidden-curriculum phrases:** "don't break your streak", "do not lose your streak", "come back every day", "play every day or", "nao percas a tua sequencia", "volta todos os dias"

### SAF-05 Understand money, purchases and chance in digital products

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** purchases.
- **Target:** Learners understand virtual currencies, real costs, in-app purchases and chance-based rewards, and can resist pressure to spend.
- **Why:** The EU KIDS Act and Digital Fairness Act proposals target spending traps and loot boxes; understanding them is consumer literacy.
- **Look for:** Explanations of virtual currency value, odds and spending pressure, in learner language.
- **Improvement:** Explain virtual currencies and chance in plain language and show real costs.
- **Ideas:** Price-tag converter from coins to euros; Odds explainer before any chance mechanic
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 2.5, 4.3
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows), [UCPD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj)
- **Hidden-curriculum phrases:** "loot box", "mystery box", "spin the wheel", "caixa mistério", "roda da sorte"

### SAF-06 Consider the environmental footprint of digital tech and AI

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ai_generative.
- **Target:** Learners know that devices, data centres and AI use energy and resources, and weigh that in their choices.
- **Why:** Protecting the environment is a DigComp competence; AILit includes comparing how AI systems consume energy and resources.
- **Look for:** Content on energy, resources, e-waste or the footprint of AI use.
- **Improvement:** Add a short activity on the energy and resource cost of the technology learners use.
- **Ideas:** Energy cost shown for each AI request in a simulation; Repair-not-replace mission
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 4.4; AILIT Engage 5; UNESCO-AIMIL 4.5
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)


## PRB: Problem solving and learning to learn

*Does it help learners solve problems, choose tools and reflect on their own digital skills?*

### PRB-01 Solve technical problems

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners identify and solve simple technical problems and know where to find help.
- **Why:** Identifying and solving technical problems is a DigComp competence.
- **Look for:** Troubleshooting tasks, hints that teach strategies rather than give answers.
- **Improvement:** Use hints that teach a strategy (check, isolate, try, ask) instead of the answer.
- **Ideas:** Fix-the-machine puzzles; Hint ladder that teaches a troubleshooting method
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 5.1
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149)

### PRB-02 Match tools to needs, including choosing not to use one

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ai_generative.
- **Target:** Learners choose a digital tool (including AI) that fits the task, and recognise when no tool or AI is the better choice.
- **Why:** DigComp asks learners to identify needs and technological responses; AILit treats deciding not to use AI as a competent choice.
- **Look for:** Tasks where learners pick between tools or decide whether to use AI, and justify it.
- **Improvement:** Add a decision step where learners choose the tool, or no tool, and explain why.
- **Ideas:** Tool-choice cards with trade-offs; Do-I-need-AI decision step before a task
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 5.2; AILIT Manage 1, Manage 2
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)

### PRB-03 Reflect on and plan one's own digital competence

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** B3, B4, B5.
- **Target:** Learners assess what they can already do, set goals and track progress in their digital competence.
- **Why:** Identifying digital competence needs is a DigComp competence; AILit strengthened metacognition and self-regulation.
- **Look for:** Self-assessment, goal setting or learner-facing progress views tied to competences.
- **Improvement:** Show learners the competence they practised and ask them to rate and plan the next step.
- **Ideas:** Skill tree that names the competence, not only the level; End-of-mission self-check
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 5.4; AILIT Manage 4
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)


## AI: AI literacy

*Does it help learners engage with, create with, manage and shape AI?*

### AI-01 Recognise AI and its influence

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ai_generative, ai_adaptive, ai_assessment, recommender.
- **Target:** Learners recognise when AI is involved and how it shapes what they see, choose and are offered.
- **Why:** AILit Engage 1 and 4; UNESCO's human-centred mindset. Recognising AI comes before judging it.
- **Look for:** Activities that make AI visible (where is the AI here?) including in the product itself.
- **Improvement:** Make AI visible in the experience and ask learners where it shapes what they see.
- **Ideas:** Where-is-the-AI hunt across everyday apps; Show what the game's own adaptive engine decided and why
- **Framework references:** AILIT Engage 1, Engage 4; UNESCO-AICFS human-centred mindset
- **Sources:** [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AICFS](https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/ai-competency-framework-students)

### AI-02 Explain how AI works, without anthropomorphism

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ai_generative.
- **Target:** Learners describe what AI systems do (predict, classify, generate) in accurate language, and that they do not think or feel.
- **Why:** AILit Engage 2 asks for language that clears up misconceptions; UNESCO warns children treat fluent AI as having a mind.
- **Look for:** Explanations of data, patterns and prediction; AI characters that say clearly what they are.
- **Improvement:** Explain how the AI works in plain words and avoid presenting it as a friend or a person.
- **Ideas:** Train-a-tiny-model unplugged activity; AI character that explains it predicts words
- **Framework references:** AILIT Engage 2; UNESCO-AIMIL 1.1, 3.1; UNESCO-AICFS AI techniques and applications
- **Sources:** [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AIMIL](https://doi.org/10.58338/JXYO3928), [UNESCO-AIAGE](https://www.unesco.org/en/digital-education)
- **Hidden-curriculum phrases:** "ai friend", "your best friend", "i am your friend", "i'm your friend", "knows everything", "always right", "never wrong", "never makes mistakes", "o teu melhor amigo", "sou teu amigo", "sabe tudo", "nunca se engana", "tem sempre razao"

### AI-03 Evaluate AI outputs: accept, revise or reject

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ai_generative.
- **Target:** Learners check AI outputs against trusted sources and task needs, and decide to accept, revise or reject them.
- **Why:** AILit Engage 3; UNESCO's three source questions for AI answers (what shaped it, what is missing, who is accountable).
- **Look for:** Tasks where AI output can be wrong and learners must verify and decide.
- **Improvement:** Build in AI answers that need checking, and make learners decide with a reason.
- **Ideas:** Planted AI mistakes to find; Accept-revise-reject buttons with a reason
- **Framework references:** AILIT Engage 3; UNESCO-AIMIL 2.5, 3.3
- **Sources:** [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AIMIL](https://doi.org/10.58338/JXYO3928)

### AI-04 Recognise bias and fairness issues

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners explain how data and design choices can make AI unfair, and how to notice it.
- **Why:** AILit Engage 6; UNESCO highlights cultural and linguistic exclusion by AI.
- **Look for:** Activities where learners compare outputs for different groups or examine training data.
- **Improvement:** Add one activity where learners find and discuss a biased result.
- **Ideas:** Biased-dataset sorting game; Compare outputs for different names or languages
- **Framework references:** AILIT Engage 6; UNESCO-AICFS ethics of AI
- **Sources:** [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AICFS](https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/ai-competency-framework-students), [UNESCO-AIAGE](https://www.unesco.org/en/digital-education)

### AI-05 Weigh ethics, values and resources of AI use

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners judge whether a use of AI fits human values and rights, including privacy, accountability and environmental cost.
- **Why:** AILit Engage 5 and 7; UNESCO's ethics of AI dimension. Ethics is part of literacy, not a separate topic.
- **Look for:** Dilemmas, debates or role plays about AI use and who is accountable.
- **Improvement:** Add a dilemma where learners argue whether and how AI should be used.
- **Ideas:** Who-answers-for-the-algorithm role play; Should-we-use-AI-here debate cards
- **Framework references:** AILIT Engage 5, Engage 7; UNESCO-AICFS ethics of AI; UNESCO-AIMIL 4.4
- **Sources:** [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AICFS](https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/ai-competency-framework-students), [UNESCO-AIMIL](https://doi.org/10.58338/JXYO3928)

### AI-06 Create with AI while keeping one's own voice

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** B4, B5. **Natural fit for:** ai_generative.
- **Target:** Learners use AI to explore ideas, get feedback and refine their work, while the work stays theirs and AI help is disclosed.
- **Why:** AILit Create 1 to 3 keep the learner's own creative vision first. UNESCO recalls a minimum age of 13 for independent use of generative AI in class.
- **Look for:** Tasks where AI gives feedback or alternatives and learners decide, with disclosure of AI use.
- **Improvement:** Make AI a feedback partner, keep the learner as author, and show what AI contributed.
- **Ideas:** AI as critic, not author; Version history showing learner and AI contributions
- **Framework references:** AILIT Create 1, Create 2, Create 3
- **Sources:** [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AIMIL](https://doi.org/10.58338/JXYO3928)
- **Hidden-curriculum phrases:** "the ai will write it for you", "ai does your homework", "no need to think", "a ia faz os trabalhos de casa", "a ia escreve por ti"

### AI-07 Decide when and how to use AI, and monitor its use

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all. **Natural fit for:** ai_generative.
- **Target:** Learners decide whether a task should be done with AI, split tasks between human and AI, and review the result.
- **Why:** AILit Manage 1 to 4; delegation and oversight are central to agency.
- **Look for:** Explicit choices about using AI, task decomposition, and review of AI contribution.
- **Improvement:** Add a decision point and a review step for every AI-assisted task.
- **Ideas:** Human-or-AI task sorter; Oversight checkpoint after each AI step
- **Framework references:** AILIT Manage 1, Manage 3, Manage 4
- **Sources:** [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)

### AI-08 Investigate and shape AI systems

- **Scope:** claimed. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners investigate how an AI system is meant to work, test it with criteria and propose improvements for human wellbeing.
- **Why:** AILit Shape 1 to 4 and UNESCO's AI system design dimension. Learners can shape technology, not only be shaped by it.
- **Look for:** Tasks where learners test, train or redesign a simple AI system, even unplugged.
- **Improvement:** Add a task where learners test an AI system with their own cases and propose a change.
- **Ideas:** Train-and-test a classifier in a sandbox; Redesign a recommender for fairness
- **Framework references:** AILIT Shape 1, Shape 2, Shape 3, Shape 4; UNESCO-AICFS AI system design
- **Sources:** [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AICFS](https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/ai-competency-framework-students)


## TRN: Transparency that teaches

*Does the product explain itself to children in a way that builds literacy, and avoid teaching the opposite?*

### TRN-01 Child-friendly explanation of how the product works and what data it uses

- **Scope:** universal. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Children get a short, age-appropriate explanation of what the product does, what data it uses and why, inside the product.
- **Why:** GDPR Art. 12 asks for clear language for children; the DSA Art. 28 guidelines and General Comment 25 ask for child-friendly information.
- **Look for:** Child-facing explainers, onboarding, or a data page written for the age band.
- **Improvement:** Write a child-facing explainer of the product and its data use, tested with the age band.
- **Ideas:** How-this-game-works card at first launch; My-data page with icons
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 4.2
- **Sources:** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation), [IEEE2089](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9627644)

### TRN-02 AI disclosure that teaches its limits

- **Scope:** feature (ai_generative, ai_adaptive, ai_assessment). **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Wherever AI is used, children are told it is AI, what it can and cannot do, and that it can be wrong, in age-appropriate words.
- **Why:** AI Act Art. 50 requires disclosure; AILit Engage 2 and 3 turn disclosure into learning; the KIDS Act proposal and UNICEF guidance ask for transparency to children.
- **Look for:** In-product AI labels and explanations of limits, written for the age band.
- **Improvement:** Add an AI label with a short explanation of what the AI does and that it can make mistakes.
- **Ideas:** I am an AI badge with a tap-to-learn explainer; Confidence hints on AI answers
- **Framework references:** AILIT Engage 2, Engage 3
- **Sources:** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [UNICEF-AI](https://www.unicef.org/innocenti/media/11996/file/UNICEF-Innocenti-Guidance-on-AI-and-Children-3-Checklist-2025.pdf), [5R-AICODE](https://5rightsfoundation.com/resource/children-ai-design-code/)

### TRN-03 Explain adaptivity and recommendations

- **Scope:** feature (ai_adaptive, recommender). **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Children and teachers can see why the product chose a level, task or item, and can change it.
- **Why:** The DSA and its Art. 28 guidelines ask for recommender transparency and choice; AILit Engage 4 teaches how recommendations shape perspectives.
- **Look for:** Why-am-I-seeing-this explanations and a way to choose differently.
- **Improvement:** Add a why-am-I-seeing-this explanation and a way to choose another path.
- **Ideas:** A why-this-level button; Learner choice to override the next task
- **Framework references:** AILIT Engage 4
- **Sources:** [DSA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)

### TRN-04 Commercial content and purchases explained as a learning moment

- **Scope:** feature (purchases). **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Every purchase, ad or sponsored item is clearly labelled with its real cost or commercial intent, in words the child understands.
- **Why:** UCPD bans direct exhortation to children; the KIDS Act and DFA proposals require real-time purchase labels and ban disguised advertising.
- **Look for:** Price labels in real money, ad and sponsorship labels, explanations for children.
- **Improvement:** Label prices in real money and mark commercial content, with a one-line explanation for children.
- **Ideas:** Coins-to-euros label on every price; This is an ad tag with a tap-to-learn note
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 1.2
- **Sources:** [UCPD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows)

### TRN-05 Provenance labels for generated or manipulated media

- **Scope:** feature (ai_generative). **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** AI-generated or altered images, audio and video are labelled, and children can learn what the label means.
- **Why:** AI Act Art. 50 requires marking of synthetic content; AILit Create 4 addresses authenticity.
- **Look for:** Labels or watermarks on generated media and an explanation for learners.
- **Improvement:** Label generated media and explain the label to learners.
- **Ideas:** Made with AI stamp that opens a short explainer; Provenance panel on shared creations
- **Framework references:** AILIT Create 4
- **Sources:** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)

### TRN-06 Safety tools explained where they are used

- **Scope:** feature (chat, multiplayer, social, ugc). **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Block, report, mute and help options are explained to children in context, so using them is itself a lesson.
- **Why:** The KIDS Act proposal (Art. 12) asks for contact safeguards and child-friendly reporting; DSA Art. 16 for notice mechanisms.
- **Look for:** Child-facing explanations next to report and block, practice flows, links to helplines.
- **Improvement:** Explain report and block in the moment, and show what happens after a report.
- **Ideas:** First-time tooltip on the report button; Practice reporting in the tutorial
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 4.1, 4.3
- **Sources:** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DSA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj), [BIK](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/strategy-better-internet-kids)

### TRN-07 No hidden curriculum

- **Scope:** universal. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** The product does not model what literacy teaches against, such as AI that claims to be a friend or to know everything, pressure loops or disguised selling.
- **Why:** Children learn from how products behave, not only from lessons. UNESCO and AILit warn about anthropomorphic AI; the KIDS Act and DFA proposals about manipulative design.
- **Look for:** Copy, dialogue and mechanics that contradict the learning goals (see the conflict phrases of every target).
- **Improvement:** Remove or rewrite the copy and mechanics flagged as conflicts, and add a review step for new content.
- **Ideas:** Review all character dialogue against AI-02; Review reward loops against SAF-04
- **Framework references:** AILIT Engage 2
- **Sources:** [UNESCO-AIAGE](https://www.unesco.org/en/digital-education), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows)

### TRN-08 Personal questions say why they are asked

- **Scope:** feature (survey). **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Before any question about their life, children read or hear why it is asked, who will see the answer and that they can skip it, so answering becomes a lesson in their own data.
- **Why:** GDPR Art. 12 and 13 ask for clear information at the moment data is collected; DigComp 4.2 asks learners to understand how their data is used. A survey is the most concrete data moment a child meets in a product.
- **Look for:** Child-facing lines before each question or set of questions, a visible skip or "prefer not to say", and a way to see one's own answers later.
- **Improvement:** Add one plain sentence per question set on why it is asked and who sees the answer, test it with the age band, and link it in the survey register.
- **Ideas:** Why-we-ask card before the questions; My-answers page the child can open and change
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 4.2
- **Sources:** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation)


## EDU: Educator and family enablement

*Can teachers and families turn use into learning, and see that learning happened?*

### EDU-01 Learning goals stated and mapped to a framework or curriculum

- **Scope:** universal. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** The product states what learners will know or be able to do, mapped to DigComp, AILit, the national curriculum or another named framework.
- **Why:** Pedagogical fit and curriculum alignment is the first EU-DEC criterion; learning goals are the starting point of EAF and EdTech for Good reviews.
- **Look for:** A list of learning goals with framework references (for example DigComp 1.2, AILit Engage 3, Aprendizagens Essenciais).
- **Improvement:** Write learning goals per activity and map each to a named framework and age band.
- **Ideas:** Goal card per mission; Curriculum map for teachers
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 all; AILIT all
- **Sources:** [EU-DEC](https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/1fa0183b-dbbe-11f0-8da2-01aa75ed71a1/language-en), [ET4G2](https://www.unicef.org/digitaleducation/edtech-for-good), [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/)

### EDU-02 Teacher guidance for before, during and after use

- **Scope:** universal. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Teachers get a guide with set-up, facilitation tips and debrief questions that link play to the literacy goals.
- **Why:** The EU-DEC guidelines and EdTech for Good stress educator judgement and professionalism; in game-based learning the debrief is where learning is made explicit.
- **Look for:** Teacher guide, lesson plans, debrief or discussion questions.
- **Improvement:** Add a teacher guide with a debrief for each literacy goal.
- **Ideas:** Three-step lesson card: frame, play, debrief; Printable discussion prompts
- **Framework references:** -
- **Sources:** [EU-DEC](https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/1fa0183b-dbbe-11f0-8da2-01aa75ed71a1/language-en), [ET4G2](https://www.unicef.org/digitaleducation/edtech-for-good), [ARNAB2014](https://doi.org/10.1111/bjet.12113)

### EDU-03 Evidence of learning beyond engagement

- **Scope:** universal. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** The product or its documentation shows how learning of the targets can be seen (formative checks, learner products, evaluation), not only time on task or points.
- **Why:** Impact and assessment is an EU-DEC criterion; EdTech for Good asks for outcome measurement beyond engagement; the Dutch 3E framework grades evidence strength.
- **Look for:** Assessment aligned to goals, evaluation plans or results, without surveillance of learners and without personal questions beyond a survey register.
- **Improvement:** Add a light formative check per goal and plan a small evaluation with a partner school, collecting evidence under the CSEF rules on personal questions (CORE-DAT-13 to 18).
- **Ideas:** Exit-ticket after each mission; Portfolio of learner decisions
- **Framework references:** AILIT learner expectations
- **Sources:** [EU-DEC](https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/1fa0183b-dbbe-11f0-8da2-01aa75ed71a1/language-en), [ET4G2](https://www.unicef.org/digitaleducation/edtech-for-good), [NL-3E](https://www.thuas.com/research/centre-expertise/3e-evidence-based-evaluation-edtech)

### EDU-04 Age-appropriate progression

- **Scope:** universal. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Literacy targets are sequenced by age band or level (basic, intermediate, advanced), and AI features respect age guidance.
- **Why:** AILit gives learner expectations at three levels; DigComp 3.0 has four proficiency levels; UNESCO asks for context-sensitive, age-appropriate AI.
- **Look for:** Progression tables, age bands per activity, and age rules for AI features.
- **Improvement:** Map each goal to an age band and level, and state age rules for AI features.
- **Ideas:** Same goal at three levels of challenge; Age gate for independent AI use
- **Framework references:** DIGCOMP3 proficiency levels; AILIT learner expectations
- **Sources:** [DIGCOMP3](https://data.europa.eu/doi/10.2760/0001149), [AILIT](https://ailiteracyframework.org/), [UNESCO-AIAGE](https://www.unesco.org/en/digital-education)

### EDU-05 Accessible and inclusive literacy learning

- **Scope:** universal. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Learners with different needs, languages and backgrounds can reach the same literacy goals.
- **Why:** Design, accessibility and inclusion is an EU-DEC criterion and an EdTech for Good pillar; the European Accessibility Act applies to many services.
- **Look for:** Accessibility features, language options, alternative paths, and testing with diverse learners.
- **Improvement:** Offer alternative paths to each goal and test with learners with diverse needs.
- **Ideas:** Read-aloud and dyslexia-friendly mode; Same mission with visual, audio or text clues
- **Framework references:** -
- **Sources:** [EU-DEC](https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/1fa0183b-dbbe-11f0-8da2-01aa75ed71a1/language-en), [ET4G2](https://www.unicef.org/digitaleducation/edtech-for-good), [EAA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj)

### EDU-06 AI literacy support for school staff

- **Scope:** feature (ai_generative, ai_adaptive, ai_assessment). **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** When the product uses AI, the provider gives schools material so staff understand what the AI does, its limits and how to oversee it.
- **Why:** AI Act Art. 4, as recast by the AI Omnibus, asks providers and deployers (often the school) to take measures supporting staff AI literacy; Art. 26 requires competent human oversight for high-risk systems.
- **Look for:** Staff guides, training, explainers of the AI and its oversight.
- **Improvement:** Provide a short staff explainer and oversight guide for every AI feature.
- **Ideas:** Ten-minute staff explainer of the AI; Oversight checklist for teachers
- **Framework references:** -
- **Sources:** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [AIA-OMNIBUS](https://fpf.org/blog/the-ai-act-implementation-timeline-what-changes-under-the-ai-omnibus), [EU-EDUPKG](https://doi.org/10.2766/6358386)

### EDU-07 Guidance for families

- **Scope:** universal. **Age bands:** all.
- **Target:** Families get short material on what the product teaches, how to talk about it at home and which settings they control.
- **Why:** The KIDS Act proposal requires tools for guardians; the Education Package's Healthy Screens Pledge links schools and families; BIK+ supports parents.
- **Look for:** Parent or guardian guides, conversation starters, family settings explained.
- **Improvement:** Add a one-page family guide with conversation starters linked to the literacy goals.
- **Ideas:** Talk-about-it card after each unit; Family settings page in plain language
- **Framework references:** -
- **Sources:** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [EU-EDUPKG](https://doi.org/10.2766/6358386), [BIK](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/strategy-better-internet-kids)
